subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity readiness — probing questions & next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@finlytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: opsai-sales@opsai.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick summary + remaining questions

Tessa, thanks again for carving out time today — that was really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can confirm fit against our compliance and performance needs.

Pain points we emphasized on the call:
- Production latency variability under load (our p95 spikes from ~120ms to >400ms during nightly batch reads).
- Lack of isolation: we cannot have customer PII/PHI co-mingled with other tenants — must run in an isolated reserved pool or VPC.
- Unpredictable burst behavior when batch jobs and real-time inference overlap — we need clear burst capacity behavior.

Current stack and constraints:
- Models: fine-tuned Llama 2 variants (7B / 13B family).
- Serving: in-house PyTorch + custom pre/post-processing.
- Typical request: 1.2k tokens on average (long tail up to 8k), avg prompt+context ~1.5MB payloads.

Success criteria we care about:
- Predictable sustained throughput: ~200 TPS sustained during business hours, spikes to ~1000 TPS for short windows.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for single-shot prompts <= 2k tokens; graceful degradation beyond that.
- Data isolation and auditability: dedicated pool with KMS integration and audit logs.

Questions we still have:
1) What dedicated pool sizes do you recommend for Llama-13B with our long-tail sequences?
2) How does Redwood handle KV cache warm-up and cold-starts — any recommendations to reduce p95 during spikes?
3) Can you confirm the autoscaling/burst policy: are we billed for reserved capacity only, and how does burst overcommit work?
4) What telemetry/logs will we get for per-request tracing and audit?

Attachments: I attached our internal traffic profile (CSV) during the call — happy to share more.

Next steps: Samira will compile the traffic +/- retention constraints and share by next week. Can Redwood send a short pilot proposal and a pricing ballpark?

Thanks,
Samira
Head of ML Engineering, FinLytics

---
Attachment: traffic_profile_sep.csv (attachment stub)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick summary + remaining questions

Samira — great to meet you and thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, our initial recommendations, and an owner-level mutual action plan so timelines are clear. I copied Karthik (serving) and Marissa (solutions) for technical + pricing follow-up.

What we heard (pain + constraints):
- Need dedicated, isolated reserved pool (PHI/PII concerns).
- Sustained ~200 TPS with bursts to ~1000 TPS.
- Model family: Llama 2 fine-tuned (7B/13B); long-tail sequences up to 8k.
- Current infra: PyTorch-based, will own pre/post-processing.

Initial recommendation (pilot-ready):
- Pilot: 3-node reserved pool (A100-class) tuned for Llama-13B, KV-cache enabled with persistent cache across requests.
- Autoscaling/burst: Configure reserved baseline to cover 200 TPS sustained; burst buffer that borrows from shared burst capacity up to 1k TPS with throttling rules at 90% of node utilization to protect p95.
- Isolation & security: Private VPC + customer KMS keys + 90-day audit log retention (can extend).
- Sequence handling: suggest truncation policy for requests >4k tokens during pilot; we’ll instrument fallback model variants for longer contexts.

Answers to your questions:
1) Pool size: For Llama-13B and your token profile, 3 x A100 (or equivalent) is a safe pilot. We’ll run a quick sizing sim once we see sample payloads.
2) KV warm-up: we use asynchronous prefix caching and recommend a short warm-up phase (5–10 minutes) for cache population; also support a pre-warm API during pilot.
3) Billing & burst: reserved capacity billed as committed baseline; burst usage beyond reserved runs on metered spot-like capacity at a higher rate. We will surface both costs in the proposal.
4) Telemetry: request-level traces, token-level cost breakdown, and SLO dashboards with exportable CSV/JSON logs (integrates with your SIEM).

Mutual action plan (owners + dates):
- FinLytics: share representative traffic logs + example long-tail prompts — owner: Samira — due: 2026-09-08.
- Redwood: produce pilot proposal (pool sizing + pricing + pilot runbook) — owner: Marissa — due: 2026-09-10.
- Redwood: run a preliminary sizing sim after logs — owner: Karthik — due: 2026-09-13.
- FinLytics & Redwood: agree on pilot window (proposed 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-24) — owner: Samira / Tessa — target: 2026-09-15.

Attachments: I attached a short capacity worksheet and a mutual action plan template to speed alignment.

If that looks right I’ll follow up with Marissa’s pilot proposal and a first-pass pricing sheet.

Thanks — talk soon.
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: capacity_model_estimate.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick summary + remaining questions

Quick technical addendum from the serving team:
- On KV-cache warm-up: besides prefix caching, we recommend a short synthetic warm-up traffic pattern that mirrors your peak token sizes; this reduces p95 by ~30% in our internal sims. We can provide a small script to generate warm-up traffic.
- Canary: propose a canary rollout that limits fractional traffic (5–10%) through the reserved pool for the first 24 hours to validate latency and model outputs.
- Throttling policy: set conservative CPU/GPU headroom triggers (e.g., 85% GPU mem / 75% SM util) to ensure graceful degradation rather than hard failures.

I’ll include the warm-up script and a sample canary config with Marissa’s proposal.

—Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Samira Khan <samira@finlytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick summary + remaining questions

Thanks, all — this is very helpful. Confirming next steps from FinLytics:
- We’ll share traffic profile + 30-day sample logs and three representative long-tail prompts by 2026-09-08 (Samira).
- We’re good with the proposed pilot window (2026-09-20 to 2026-09-24) pending final pricing.
- Please include an estimate for committed reserved pricing vs metered burst so our procurement team can review.

One small ask: can Redwood include a short note in the pilot runbook describing how you enforce tenant isolation when nodes host multiple workloads (if they do at all)? We need that language for our security review.

Appreciate the quick turn — looking forward to Marissa’s proposal.

Samira
Head of ML Engineering, FinLytics
